title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: A volatile week ended with a tech-led selloff Friday — the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.1% as worries resurfaced over returns on AI infrastructure spending; CoreWeave sank 11.9% on the day (down >23% for the week).

Markets: Brent crude jumped 3.7% to near $110/bbl, its highest since May, helping push the 10-year Treasury yield up to 5.1% (still below its recent ~5.3% high) on renewed inflation concerns; gold rose to ~$4,189/oz.

Companies: Tesla unveiled its flight-capable Roadster (with SpaceX-designed thrusters) to a tepid reception, with shares down ~2.1%; Barclays analysts say the stunt points to a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger as soon as this fall, with AI cited as a driver.

Companies: Apple and Meta struck a notable AI détente — Meta's new open-weight "Muse Spark Open" model (816B parameters) will run locally on Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studios, a rare collaboration between the longtime rivals.
Companies: A corporate pushback is building against the SEC's stock-tokenization push, with Broadcom, Verizon and others objecting over fears it could fragment pricing and create a shadow market.

Macro/Policy: Wall Street's AI-debt anxiety is intensifying — projected AI infrastructure capex ($7T through 2030) far outstrips expected revenue (~$3.6T, per Gartner); AI-related debt issuance plunged to $23B in September from $113B in June, and JPMorgan's Dimon says the bank is tightening credit as an Oracle data-center loan and Nvidia-backed Firmus's shelved IPO show rising stress.
